The increasing availability of genomic data made L56@P0: clear that the ‘DXP-independent’ route is wide-spread L57@P0: among archaea, plants, fungi and most bacteria including L58@P0: the tubercle bacillus (Mittenhuber, 2001). Remarkably, L59@P0: about 4% of all classified enzymes depend on PLP as L60@P0: cofactor, highlighting the enormous functional diversity of L61@P0: the vitamin (Mozzarelli and Bettati, 2006; Fitzpatrick et al., L62@P0: 2007). M. tuberculosis possesses 58 genes encoding proteins that carry a PLP binding motif (Cole et al., 1998; L63@P0: Percudani and Peracchi, 2009). Out of those genes 21 L64@P0: were identified as essential for growth in vitro and most of L65@P0: them are functionally related to the amino acid metabolism (Sassetti et al., 2003). Further implications of PLP in L66@P0: mycobacteria include the biosynthesis of vitamins B7 L67@P0: (biotin), B9 (folate) and B12 (cobalamin), the formation of L68@P0: cell wall components and building blocks of DNA (Cole L69@P0: et al., 1998; Strych et al., 2001; Percudani and Peracchi, L70@P0: 2009). In addition, vitamin B6 was reported to be a potent L71@P0: quencher of reactive oxygen intermediates (Ehrenshaft L72@P0: et al., 1999; Jain and Lim, 2001; Matxain et al., 2009).
